catalog_card_blurb: Tesamorelin is a 44-residue synthetic analogue of human growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), also referenced as TH-9507. Veracue supplies Tesamorelin Spray as a research material for laboratory work. The most directly relevant published evidence comes from clinical trials of EGRIFTA WR, the FDA-approved subcutaneous injectable studied in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy — human clinical evidence, but for a different formulation and route than this spray. No spray-specific clinical or preclinical evidence was identified, so this material does not establish an effect, safety profile, or dosing in people.

1_hero.body: Tesamorelin is a 44-residue synthetic analogue of human growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), studied for its role in GHRH-receptor signaling and the downstream growth hormone/IGF-1 axis. Tesamorelin Spray is Veracue's research-grade material built around this compound, supplied strictly for laboratory use. It is a separate research product from EGRIFTA WR, the FDA-approved subcutaneous injectable tesamorelin product — this page keeps that line clear throughout.

3_what_is_tesamorelin.heading: What Is Tesamorelin?
3_what_is_tesamorelin.body: Tesamorelin is a synthetic peptide built on the 44-amino-acid sequence of human growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), with a trans-3-hexenoic acid group added at the N-terminus. That modification is what distinguishes it from native GHRH — it's reported to make the peptide more resistant to enzymatic breakdown, which is part of why it became a viable candidate for pharmaceutical development. Tesamorelin is the active compound in EGRIFTA WR, an FDA-approved subcutaneous injectable — a distinct pharmaceutical product with its own formulation, indication, and regulatory status, separate from the Veracue research material described here.

4_scientific_identity.heading: Scientific Identity
4_scientific_identity.amino_acid_length: 44 residues, C-terminally amidated, matching the human GHRH(1-44) backbone
4_scientific_identity.note: The N-terminal trans-3-hexenoic acid modification is the single structural difference from native human GHRH(1-44); this is what's referenced by the sequence and reference identity above, not a separate salt or product-specific form.

5_mechanism.heading: How Is Tesamorelin Studied in Growth-Hormone Signaling Research?
5_mechanism.body: Tesamorelin is studied as an agonist of the GHRH receptor (GHRHR) on pituitary somatotroph cells. GHRH-receptor activation is associated in the literature with pulsatile growth hormone release, and researchers commonly track circulating IGF-1 as a downstream pharmacodynamic marker in tesamorelin studies. Published research examining body-composition endpoints — particularly visceral adipose tissue — has looked at this signaling pathway in the context of the approved injectable formulation. That mechanistic and clinical picture describes the tesamorelin molecule and EGRIFTA WR specifically; it isn't a description of the Veracue Spray's own behavior in a research system, which hasn't been characterized as its own formulation.

6_clinical_evidence.heading: What Does the Tesamorelin Research Actually Show?
6_clinical_evidence.body: The clinical evidence for tesamorelin centers on EGRIFTA WR, a subcutaneous injectable studied in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy. Trials supporting FDA approval measured reduction in visceral adipose tissue in that population. The label is specific about the boundaries of that finding: long-term cardiovascular safety hasn't been established, and the product is not indicated for weight-loss management, since it has a reported weight-neutral effect. Tesamorelin's broader literature also covers GHRH-receptor pharmacodynamics — GH and IGF-1 response — independent of the lipodystrophy indication. No tesamorelin spray-specific clinical or preclinical evidence was identified in the literature reviewed for this page; the evidence above describes the injectable route and the studied population, not a spray-format research material.

subsections.heading: Terminology: Tesamorelin and TH-9507
subsections.body: Tesamorelin and TH-9507 refer to the same molecule — TH-9507 was its development-stage designation before approval. You'll see both used interchangeably across supplier and research literature.

subsections.heading: Molecule vs. Product Specification
subsections.body: The name 'Tesamorelin Spray' identifies the active compound and product category, not its concentration, vehicle, or route. Section 11 lists exactly which formulation details are confirmed and which aren't — don't infer a route or dose from the product name itself.

subsections.heading: Approved Injectable vs. Research Spray
subsections.body: EGRIFTA WR is an FDA-approved subcutaneous injectable with its own dosing, safety data, and regulatory status. Tesamorelin Spray is a separate, unapproved research material. Evidence generated for one doesn't carry over to the other.

subsections.heading: Reading Evidence by Model Type
subsections.body: The table above labels each finding by where it came from — human trial data for the approved injectable versus mechanistic pharmacodynamic research. subsections.heading: Purity, Assay, and Biological Activity
subsections.body: HPLC purity tells you how much of a sample is the intended compound relative to impurities. Assay confirms how much material is present relative to the labeled amount. Neither is a measure of biological activity — they're analytical chemistry results, not a statement about how a compound performs in a research system.

subsections.body: A large share of public search interest in tesamorelin concerns dosage and administration. 9_tesamorelin_vs_sermorelin.heading: Tesamorelin vs. Sermorelin
9_tesamorelin_vs_sermorelin.body: Sermorelin is GRF(1-29)-NH2 — the first 29 amino acids of human GHRH. Tesamorelin uses the full 44-residue sequence with the added trans-3-hexenoic acid modification for greater resistance to enzymatic breakdown. Both are studied as GHRH-receptor agonists, but they're distinct molecules with different sequence lengths, developed and evaluated through separate research and clinical programs. This comparison is for scientific clarity only, not a ranking or a recommendation.

10_tesamorelin_vs_ipamorelin.heading: Tesamorelin vs. Ipamorelin
10_tesamorelin_vs_ipamorelin.body: Tesamorelin and ipamorelin both come up in growth-hormone research, but they work through different receptors. Tesamorelin is a GHRH analogue studied as a GHRH-receptor (GHRHR) agonist. Ipamorelin is a pentapeptide studied as a selective ghrelin/GHS-receptor agonist — a mechanistically distinct pathway that also converges on growth hormone release. This page doesn't describe them as a stack or combination protocol; each has its own evidence base.

12_coa.heading: How to Read a Tesamorelin COA
12_coa.body: A complete COA for a tesamorelin research material confirms identity (typically by mass spectrometry and/or HPLC retention time against a reference standard), reports purity by HPLC, states assayed quantity against the labeled amount, and records the lot number, analysis date, and testing laboratory. For a formulated product, it should also document formulation-relevant details for that specific batch. No lot-specific COA is currently published for Tesamorelin Spray — this section will link directly to it once available.

13_what_research_does_not_establish.heading: What the Research Does Not Establish
points: Evidence generated with the approved injectable doesn't establish the pharmacokinetics, safety, or effect of a spray-format research material.
The clinical evidence base is specific to HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy evaluated for excess abdominal fat — not weight loss generally, and not other populations.
GHRH-receptor mechanistic evidence doesn't by itself establish a specific clinical outcome.
A certificate of analysis documents a specific lot's chemistry — it's separate from, and doesn't substitute for, the published clinical literature.

14_ruo.heading: Research Use Only
14_ruo.body: Tesamorelin Spray is supplied strictly for laboratory research. It is not for human or veterinary administration, not a weight-loss or wellness product, not a treatment for any condition, and not a dietary supplement. Nothing on this page is medical advice, and the published tesamorelin literature — including data on the approved injectable — is discussed here as scientific literature, not as a description of this research material's effects.

items.q: How many amino acids are in tesamorelin?
items.a: 44 residues, matching the length of native human GHRH(1-44), with a C-terminal amide.

items.q: What is the tesamorelin peptide sequence?
What is the molecular weight of tesamorelin?
How does tesamorelin relate to GHRH?
items.a: Tesamorelin is a direct structural analogue of human GHRH, using the same 44-residue sequence with an N-terminal modification for stability, and is studied as an agonist of the GHRH receptor (GHRHR).
GHRH-receptor pharmacodynamics — GH and IGF-1 response — and, for the approved injectable, clinical outcomes in visceral fat reduction among HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy.

items.q: What is known about tesamorelin clinical research?
items.a: Trials supporting FDA approval evaluated the subcutaneous injectable in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy, measuring visceral fat reduction; the label states long-term cardiovascular safety hasn't been established and the product isn't indicated for weight-loss management.

items.q: Is Tesamorelin Spray the same as approved tesamorelin injection?
items.a: No. Tesamorelin Spray is a separate, unapproved research material — it shouldn't be assumed to share EGRIFTA WR's formulation, route, concentration, or safety profile.

items.q: How is tesamorelin different from sermorelin?
items.a: Sermorelin is the shorter GRF(1-29)-NH2 fragment of GHRH; tesamorelin uses the full 44-residue sequence with an added stability modification. Both are GHRH-receptor agonists but are distinct molecules.

items.q: How is tesamorelin different from ipamorelin?
items.a: Tesamorelin acts on the GHRH receptor; ipamorelin is a pentapeptide studied as a selective ghrelin/GHS-receptor agonist — a different receptor pathway entirely.

items.q: What should a Tesamorelin COA contain?
items.a: Identity confirmation, HPLC purity, assayed quantity, lot number, analysis date, and testing laboratory. No lot-specific COA is published for this product yet.
Purity, typically reported by HPLC, is the proportion of a sample that's the intended compound relative to detectable impurities — a separate metric from assayed quantity or biological activity.

items.q: What does Research Use Only mean for Tesamorelin Spray?
items.a: The product is supplied strictly for laboratory research — not for human or veterinary use, self-administration, or any therapeutic purpose.
